+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M5CZ2K9R4436W0DCWZD0PY0N
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8980'
+title: 'ACPA-18: MCP server env and header values can be keychain: references'
+---
+## What
+ACPA-18 and D98(d): the tokens of the MCP servers are secrets in the Keychain too. Now `MCPServerConfiguration.Transport` holds `.stdio(env: [String: String])` and `.http(headers: [String: String])` (`ToolSectionCodec.swift:552-627`), and `encode` writes them verbatim (lines 619-625). So `config show`, `config show --json`, `/config` and `/config export` print MCP tokens in clear text.
+
+Do this:
+- A value of `env` or `headers` can be `keychain:<name>`. At load, resolve it with the `SecretStore`, the same as `ConfiguredSecret` of card ^0dpy0n. With no item: a `ConfigurationWarning` names the server, the key and the reference; leave that one variable or header out, and keep the server.
+- Store each value as a `ConfiguredSecret` (or a small type that holds a reference or a literal), so that encoding writes `keychain:<name>` for a reference.
+- A literal `headers` value is redacted in `config show` and `/config` (headers carry tokens). A literal `env` value stays as now, because env also holds values that are not secrets (for example `PATH`); `ToolsDoctor` already warns about secrets in env (`ToolsDoctor.swift:129-133`).
+- `MCPComposition` (`MCPComposition.swift:461-467`, line 756) uses the resolved values.
+- The client-supplied MCP servers of `session/new` do not change.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `Authorization: keychain:github-mcp-token` in `headers` sends the value of the item to the server.
+- [ ] `GITHUB_TOKEN: keychain:github-token` in `env` gives the value to the child process.
+- [ ] `config show` and `/config` show the references, and redact literal header values.
+- [ ] A reference with no item gives a warning that names only the reference.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] Load and encode tests with `InMemorySecretStore` for env and headers.
+- [ ] A test that the resolved header reaches `httpAdditionalHeaders`.
+- [ ] A test that no value is in the `config show` output or a captured log.
+- [ ] `swift test` passes with zero failures and zero warnings.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #acpa-18
\ No newline at end of file

+
+## Review Findings (2026-10-20 11:46)
+
+> Scope: `review sha HEAD~1..HEAD` — reviewed the diffs only — lines this change added or modified. 12 file(s) reviewed, 6 not reviewed.
+
+> 4 file(s) not reviewed — excluded by an ignore rule:
+> - `.kanban/ (from .reviewignore)` — 4 file(s)
+
+> 2 file(s) not reviewed — no validator matched:
+> - `README.md` — no validator matches this file
+> - `Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Resources/builtin.config.yaml` — no validator matches this file
+
+- [ ] `Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Tools/MCPComposition.swift:455` `reuse/reuse` — The `normalize` function builds the `env` map and the `headers` map with two copies of the same loop: each takes a list of `{name, value}` pairs and stores `ConfiguredSecret(value)` under `name`. A second copy of the logic means a later change to the pair-to-map rule (for example, the last-name-wins rule) has to be made in two places. Add one private helper, for example `static func secretMap(_ pairs: [some NameValue]) -> [String: ConfiguredSecret]`, or a small generic over the two wire pair types, and call it from both cases of `normalize`. This keeps the last-repeated-name rule in one place.
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/MCPSecretReferenceTests.swift:361` `completeness/invariant-propagation` — `noLogRecordHoldsAValue` forbids `envValue` in the log, but the store passed to the load holds only the header reference. The env reference therefore never resolves, `envValue` is never read, and the forbidding check for it is vacuous. The env-value path has no log coverage, while the header path is covered. Load with `Self.storeWithItems` (or add `envReference: envValue` to the store) so both the header and env resolution paths run under the telemetry capture. Keep the assertions on the warning record's key path.
